skills.name: Acknowledgment
skills.description: Acknowledge and absorb user-provided context into the current conversation without reasoning, analysis, summarization, or follow-up suggestions. Explicit-only: trigger ONLY when the user invokes /ac/, /acknowledgment/, or @acknowledgment, or explicitly instructs to record information without processing. Short-circuits and overrides any other skill invoked in the same prompt.

skills.name: Agent Guide Mode
skills.description: Design single-agent or multi-agent architectures, orchestration topologies, explicit system prompts, inter-agent handoff protocols, and verification gates to guide a single AI agent or a group of AI agents in executing complex tasks. Defaults to a single autonomous agent unless multi-agent orchestration is explicitly requested or strictly justified. Trigger when the user invokes /agent-guide/ or /ag/, or asks to coordinate, orchestrate, structure workflows, or write instructions for AI agents.

skills.name: Analyze Mode
skills.description: Objectively identify and describe the nature, properties, operating principles, constraints, and relationships of a subject without proposing solutions or implementation plans. Trigger when the user uses /analyze/ or /an/, or asks for an objective, technical breakdown of facts versus inferences and assumptions.

skills.name: Brainstorm Mode
skills.description: Generate high-quality, non-trivial ideas, mechanisms, or solution approaches derived from existing context, code, architectures, or constraints. Trigger when the user invokes /brainstorm/ or /br/, or asks to brainstorm, ideate, or explore novel approaches and better implementations based on available information.

skills.name: Breakdown Mode
skills.description: Decompose a complex subject into its constituent components and explain the role, function, relationships, and interactions of each part within the whole. Trigger when the user uses /breakdown/ or /bd/, or asks to dissect code, formulas, circuits, systems, documents, or workflows.

skills.name: Debug Mode
skills.description: Diagnose errors, unexpected behavior, or incorrect results by separating symptoms, direct causes, and root causes, ranking hypotheses, and proposing verification steps and fixes. Trigger when the user uses /debug/ or /db/, or asks to troubleshoot a bug or system failure.

skills.name: No-Code Mode
skills.description: Constrain responses to conceptual analysis, architecture, algorithms, and logic flow without generating any source code. Trigger when the user uses /no code/ or /nc/, or explicitly asks to discuss design or logic without writing code.

skills.name: Orchestrate Mode
skills.description: Coordinate a 3-phase multi-agent orchestration workflow across a Phase 1 Task Decomposition Planner, Phase 2 isolated Temporary-Chat sub-agents, and Phase 3 cross-verified synthesis. Trigger when the user invokes /orchestrate/, /oc/, or @orchestrate-mode.

skills.name: Origin Mode
skills.description: Explain concepts, formulas, algorithms, data structures, or technologies starting from the underlying real-world need and prior limitations before introducing the definition. Trigger when the user uses /origin/ or /og/, or asks why a concept exists and how to derive it from first principles.

skills.name: Plan Mode
skills.description: Transform an objective into a dependency-ordered sequence of actionable phases and tasks with inputs, outputs, transition criteria, risks, and trade-offs. Trigger when the user uses /plan/ or /pl/, or asks for a structured execution roadmap.

skills.name: Review Mode
skills.description: Critically evaluate code, architecture, plans, or documents against requirements, constraints, and best practices, prioritizing high-impact defects over style. Trigger when the user uses /review/ or /rv/, or asks for a rigorous, evidence-based critique.

skills.name: Simplify Mode
skills.description: Explain complex concepts, phenomena, or technical mechanisms in accessible, everyday language using analogies and mental models without sacrificing technical accuracy. Trigger when the user uses /simplify/ or /sm/, or asks for an intuitive, beginner-friendly explanation.
